# controller

`gamepad::unstable::controller::runtime`, `context`, `clock`, `diagnostic_sink`, `errc`, and tracing macros coordinate controller timing, diagnostics, lifecycle management, engine integration, and subsystem ownership.

## Contents

### Timing and Diagnostics

- [clock.hpp](./clock.hpp) defines `clock`, `timestamp`, `seconds`, `milliseconds`, and `latency_span` for monotonic controller timing.
- [clock.cpp](./clock.cpp) implements `clock::since_epoch()` with a thread-safe function-local epoch.
- [diagnostic.hpp](./diagnostic.hpp) defines `facility`, `severity`, `diagnostic`, `diagnostic_sink`, `logging_sink`, and `report`.
- [diagnostic.cpp](./diagnostic.cpp) implements `to_string(facility)`, `to_string(severity)`, `logging_sink::consume`, and diagnostic `report`.
- [error.hpp](./error.hpp) defines `errc`, `to_string(errc)`, stream serialization, and cold-path `error`.
- [error.cpp](./error.cpp) implements stable `errc` string tokens and `error` construction.
- [context.hpp](./context.hpp) defines the borrowed service view with `diagnostics()`, `developer()`, and device-scoped reporting.
- [context.cpp](./context.cpp) forwards `context::report` calls to controller diagnostic sinks.

### Runtime Coordination

- [runtime.hpp](./runtime.hpp) defines non-copyable `runtime`, subsystem ownership, engine lifecycle methods, frame state, and integration accessors.
- [runtime.cpp](./runtime.cpp) implements discovery, driver polling, calibration, publication, input dispatch, view latching, dvar initialization, and PlayStation light-bar output.

### Optional Instrumentation

- [trace.hpp](./trace.hpp) defines `trace::enabled`, `CONTROLLER_ZONE`, and `CONTROLLER_FRAME_MARK` as optional profiling hooks.

## Subdirectories

- [aim/](./aim/) contains aim calibration, response curves, deadzones, filtering, lock-on, and turn integration.
- [calibration/](./calibration/) contains profile measurement, normalization, validation, and persistence.
- [device/](./device/) contains device identity, capability classification, discovery, registry, and transport bindings.
- [driver/](./driver/) contains XInput and PlayStation polling, report decoding, output encoding, and driver reconciliation.
- [engine/](./engine/) contains dvars, commands, key dispatch, bindings, view movement, imports, and hooks.
- [mapping/](./mapping/) contains physical-to-engine key translation, logical commands, glyphs, bindings, and stick layouts.
- [sample/](./sample/) contains raw and canonical samples, buttons, axes, triggers, motion, touch, frames, and SPSC rings.
- [support/](./support/) contains shared controller type aliases and non-owning `function_ref`.
- [transport/](./transport/) contains HID I/O, device notifications, and dynamically loaded XInput APIs.

## Architecture / Data Flow

`runtime::frame()` invokes `discovery::scan()`, `driver::set::reconcile()`, `runtime::advance()`, `engine::key_dispatcher::dispatch()`, `engine::view_driver::observe()`, and `runtime::apply_light_bar()`.

`driver::driver::poll()` writes `sample::raw_sample`, `calibration::apply()` writes `sample::canonical_sample`, and `runtime::advance()` publishes `sample::input_frame` with `clock::timestamp`, `clock::latency_span`, `device_id`, and monotonic `sequence`.

`context` shares `diagnostic_sink`, `developer`, `errc`, and device identity values across `device`, `driver`, `sample`, `aim`, and `engine` layers without owning subsystem state.

`runtime::engine_ready()` registers engine dvars and commands, applies `binds_`, performs eager discovery, and gates subsequent `runtime::frame()` execution through `engine_ready_`.

`runtime::active_` selects one device for singular key and view state, while `runtime::latest_`, `sequence_`, `last_published_`, and `had_device_` preserve publication and takeover invariants.

## API Surface

`runtime::runtime`, `runtime::engine_ready`, `runtime::frame`, `runtime::active`, `runtime::latest`, `runtime::keys`, `runtime::binds`, `runtime::view`, `runtime::driving`, `runtime::dvars`, and `runtime::device_count` define the process-level controller boundary.

`context::make_context`, `context::diagnostics`, `context::developer`, and both `context::report` overloads define the borrowed service boundary.

`clock::now`, `clock::since_epoch`, `latency_span::latency`, `to_string(facility)`, `to_string(severity)`, `to_string(errc)`, `operator<<(ostream&, errc)`, and `report` define shared timing and diagnostic utilities.

## Behavioral Contracts

`clock::base` must satisfy `base::is_steady`, and `clock::since_epoch()` uses a first-call-fixed epoch.

`latency_span::latency()` computes `consumed - acquired` without validation and assumes `consumed >= acquired`.

`to_string(facility)` recognizes `runtime`, `discovery`, `transport`, `driver`, `decode`, `sample`, `calibration`, `mapping`, `aim`, `steam`, `engine`, and `debug`, with unknown values returning `"runtime"`.

`to_string(severity)` maps `info`, `warning`, and `error`, with unknown values returning `"info"`.

`logging_sink::consume` emits `controller: <facility>: <message> [<code>] device=<id>\n`; `[<code>]` is omitted for `errc::none`, and `device=<id>` is omitted for empty devices.

`errc` string tokens remain stable: `"none"`, `"device-unavailable"`, `"ambiguous-identity"`, `"unsupported-device"`, `"transport-failure"`, `"report-malformed"`, `"report-truncated"`, `"checksum-mismatch"`, `"output-rejected"`, `"calibration-invalid"`, `"calibration-version"`, `"graph-invalid"`, `"binding-invalid"`, `"steam-unavailable"`, `"steam-unsuitable"`, `"hook-failed"`, and `"dvar-registration"`.

`runtime::engine_ready()` is idempotent through `engine_ready_`, and `runtime::frame()` must not throw across the engine ABI or allocate on per-frame acquisition.

`runtime::profile_for()` indexes `profiles_` by `controller::family`, with `profiles_` sized for five families and a `static_assert` covering `controller::family::dualsense_edge == 4`.

`runtime::advance()` aborts publication when `driver::driver::poll()` returns `false`, increments `sequence_`, and preserves monotonic `last_published_`.

`runtime::frame()` releases held keys when `active_ != latest_.device`, while `engine::key_dispatcher::dispatch()` continues held-button repeats when `had_device_` is true.

`runtime::apply_light_bar()` clamps RGB channels to `[0, 255]`, packs `colour` as `(r << 16) | (g << 8) | b`, and submits output only when `lit_device_` or `lit_colour_` changes.

`light_bar_r`, `light_bar_g`, and `light_bar_b` default to `196`, `151`, and `54`; light-bar output requires `capability::light_bar`.

`LIBIW4X_CONTROLLER_TRACE` defaults to `0`, while `CONTROLLER_ZONE(name)` and `CONTROLLER_FRAME_MARK()` expand to `do {} while (false)` when tracing is disabled.
